dedupe_keys.name: physical attacks on the railway system dzsf dataset

description: This dataset from the German Centre for Rail Transport Research (DZSF) at the Federal Railway Authority lists physical attacks on railway systems since the railway's invention, up to 2022. Each record gives the date, location with country, state, city, coordinates and railway line, the attacker type and group, whether it was state-backed, the targets hit (tracks, bridges, stations, rolling stock, passengers, communication and other infrastructure), the means of attack (explosives, knives or batons, obstacles, fire, rail manipulation, firearms, suicide bombers, gas, hacking, missiles) and the impact. The single spreadsheet (xlsx, about 60 kB, about 1,100 rows on the main sheet plus a second sheet) was published on 31 May 2023 through the FID move research data portal for mobility and transport research, and is free under CC0. Caveats: the portal gives only a one-line description, so the sources and selection rules behind the compilation are not documented there; coverage of older and non-European events is likely uneven; and it includes a hacker category although the title names physical attacks. The data support hazard exposure and resilience studies of rail networks against sabotage and terrorism, such as estimating attack frequencies by target type; related records are ERA RINF and the Danish railway event database.
